olivia: Quick async check — we're finalizing the /v2/generate contract and ran into a couple of subtle interactions between `stop`, `max_tokens`, and `logprobs`. Can folks confirm intended behavior? cc @sam @jin :eyes:

olivia: Questions are: 1) If a stop sequence is matched, does `max_tokens` counting stop at the token boundary before the stop or include the stop tokens? 2) When streaming, if we cut because of `max_tokens` vs because of `stop`, do we still emit `logprobs` for the trailing partial token (where the stream truncated)? 3) How should `temperature`/`top_p` be interpreted if we fall back to a cheaper model variant mid-request (dedicated routing fallback)?

sam: short answers first: 1) stop wins — we should cease generation when stop is matched, and max_tokens is a hard cap. Practically we count produced tokens up to but not including bytes matched by the stop seq. 2) partial-token logprobs: we try to avoid exposing partial token probs, but streaming may include a trailing token with incomplete whitespace — behavior should be documented. 3) fallback preserves sampling params; we don't re-normalize temp/top_p across model variants, but we do annotate in the response metadata if model changed.

jin: nit: we need to be precise about where we define "token boundaries" in the contract. For BPE it's ambiguous for some unicode sequences. Recommend we say "token as defined by model tokenizer used for the final emitted model" and add a compatibility note.

ravi: practical test I ran — curl below; when `stop` matched mid-word the server returned a final chunk with text trimmed but `logprobs` absent for the last token. Repro:

```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v2/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"rwd-medium-v1","prompt":"Write the word: elephant","max_tokens":5,"stop":["phant"],"logprobs":5}'
```

ravi: result was truncated after "ele" and logprobs was empty for that trailing piece. Not sure if that's our runtime or tokenizer mismatch.

carla: From a docs POV we should show 2 examples: explicit stop earlier than max_tokens and explicit cutoff by max_tokens. Also call out streaming vs non-streaming differences. I'll add examples in the PR if we settle the semantics.

olivia: Thanks — @sam does that align with the behavior expected for backward compatibility with v1? We can't surprise customers who assumed `logprobs` is always present when requested.

sam: Good point. v1 returned logprobs up to the last fully emitted token; streaming differences existed but weren't ideal. For v2 we should: (a) guarantee `logprobs` for all fully-emitted tokens, (b) if streaming truncates a token we include a boolean `truncated_token` flag in metadata and omit logprobs for that token, (c) include `final_reason` field: one of `stop`, `max_tokens`, `eos`, `fallback-model`. That keeps it explicit and backwards-compatible if we document the new flag.

jin: Agree. Also add `model_switch` metadata when fallback occurs with original sampling params echoed and a note if params were not exactly reproducible on fallback.

olivia: Sounds good. Can someone drop a short JSON schema snippet for the response we want? I'll put it in the PR description.

carla: I sketched this earlier, simplified:
```
{
  "id":"...",
  "model":"rwd-medium-v1",
  "choices":[{
    "text":"...",
    "logprobs":{...} || null,
    "truncated_token": false
  }],
  "final_reason":"stop",
  "meta":{
    "fallback_model": null,
    "sampling_params": {"temperature":0.7,"top_p":0.9}
  }
}
```

carla: That keeps `logprobs` nullable and adds flags.

ravi: PR is https://git.company.com/redwood/inference/pull/456 — I pushed tests that reproduce the mid-token stop case. @sam can you review the runtime change (small patch to kvcache flush logic) and the contract text?

sam: Will review today. Quick heads-up: if we mark `truncated_token` agggressively some downstreams might break (they expect logprobs always). We should version the schema (response_version) so clients can opt in.

deploy-bot: Canary deploy scheduled: inference-canary-2026-03-17 @ 18:30 UTC. Will run integ tests after deploy. :rocket:

olivia: Excellent. Action items I have: 1) @sam review runtime + schema compat note, 2) @jin add tokenizer sentence to contract, 3) @carla add example snippets to docs, 4) @ravi follow up on tests failing in canary. I'll update PR with the `final_reason` enum and `truncated_token` semantics.

sam: ack, will prioritize review.

jin: ack — will add the tokenizer paragraph.
